data_controls: Verify the signature against the raw request body before parsing or processing.
Store only the minimum webhook payload fields needed for audit and replay; redact secrets and sensitive payment data from logs.
Apply existing retention and encryption controls to webhook events.
failure_handling: Persist and atomically claim event_id before applying payment state changes.
Treat an already successfully processed event_id as success and return 2xx without repeating side effects.
Validate event type, schema, payment identity, amount, currency, and allowed state transition before mutation.
Return non-2xx for invalid signatures and retryable processing failures; return 2xx for unsupported but authenticated event types when no retry can help.
Commit the idempotency record and payment-state mutation in one transaction where possible; otherwise use a durable inbox and retry-safe state transition.
Do not acknowledge with 2xx until required durable processing has completed.
observability: Emit structured logs containing event_id, event type, payment identifier, processing outcome, duplicate status, and retryable classification without sensitive payload data.
Record counters for received, processed, duplicate, rejected-signature, ignored, and failed events.
Measure processing latency and alert on sustained failures, signature failures, backlog growth, and repeated delivery attempts.
Preserve an auditable event-processing status and error reason for reconciliation.
